title: How to Measure for Carpet: Rolls, Seams and Waste Factor Explained
meta: How to measure for carpet like an installer: 12-foot rolls, seam placement and a 10 to 20 percent waste factor. A worked Everett example from Wills Flooring.
keywords: how to measure for carpet, carpet waste factor, carpet roll width 12 feet, how much carpet do I need for stairs, carpet square yards calculator, measuring a room for carpet with seams

blocks.lead: Measure each room at its longest and widest points, add three to six inches to each, then lay those rectangles against a 12-foot-wide roll. Real homes need 10 to 20 percent more carpet than their square footage.
blocks.detail: The extra is the strips left over when a 12-foot roll meets an 11-foot room, plus seams that have to run with the pile. That waste is carpet you buy, not labor you pay for: our installation labor is $0.99 per sq ft of measured floor, plus $30 per step. Here is how both numbers come out of one Everett two-story.

blocks.html: A common Reddit thread goes: "My rooms total 640 square feet, the store says I need 790, are they ripping me off?" Usually not. Carpet is a 12-foot-wide product cut to fit rooms that are almost never 12 feet wide, and the offcuts are real. In the Silver Lake and Eastmont two-stories we carpet most often, the layout on the roll decides the yardage. That math lets you check any quote, including ours.

blocks.text: Measure like an installer, not a painter

items.text: Measure each room at its longest and widest points, wall to wall. Closets are their own rectangles, door opening included.
Add three inches to each dimension for trimming, six if the walls are out of square, as in most 1920s Riverside houses.
Every room becomes a piece cut from a 12-foot roll. A room 11 ft 6 in wide fits one width. A 13 ft room needs a full width plus a seamed fill strip.
A standard stair uses about 20 inches of length with the tuck. Thirteen stairs is about 22 feet, in a strip 3 inches wider than the stair.
Add the piece lengths, multiply by 12 for square feet, divide by 9 for square yards. Compare to the plain square footage and you have the waste factor.

blocks.text: Worked example: a Silver Lake two-story

items.title: What we measured
items.text: Primary bedroom 13 ft × 15 ft. Kids' bedrooms 11 ft × 12 ft and 10 ft × 11 ft. Hall 3 ft × 14 ft. Two closets, 2 ft × 5 ft. Straight staircase, 13 steps, 3 ft wide. Plain square footage: 195 + 132 + 110 + 42 + 20 = 499 sq ft, plus stairs.

items.title: How it cuts from a 12 ft roll
items.text: Primary bedroom: one 15 ft 6 in length plus a 1 ft 3 in fill strip seamed along one side, cut from a second 15 ft 6 in length. The rest of that length yields the hall and closets. Bedrooms two and three: 12 ft 6 in and 11 ft 6 in lengths.

items.title: Strips across the roll
items.text: Stairs 3 ft wide need strips 3 ft 3 in wide, so three fit across a 12 ft roll. Thirteen steps at 20 inches is about 22 feet, or 7 ft 4 in per strip. One 7 ft 6 in length covers them.

items.title: Roll length and waste
items.text: 15 ft 6 in + 15 ft 6 in + 12 ft 6 in + 11 ft 6 in + 7 ft 6 in = 62 ft 6 in of roll. Times 12 ft is 750 sq ft, about 83 sq yd, against 499 sq ft of floor plus 65 sq ft of stairs. Waste lands near 25 percent, thanks to the 13 ft bedroom and the hall.

blocks.note: Swap the primary bedroom to 11 ft 6 in wide and the waste drops under 15 percent. Room width relative to 12 feet is the whole game.

blocks.title: What that house pays in labor:
blocks.text: 499 sq ft of floor sits just under our 500 sq ft minimum, so labor bills at 500 × $0.99 = $495, plus 13 × $30 = $390 for the staircase, plus 500 × $0.45 = $225 to pull and haul the old carpet and pad. That is $1,110 of labor on a job that orders about 83 sq yd. The 25 percent waste lands in the carpet and pad price, quoted at the estimate, not in ours.
Seam rules that decide the layout

items.html: Seams run toward the main light source. A seam across a window's light casts a shadow line. In a Port Gardner condo with one wall of glass, that fixes the direction of every piece.
Pile direction must match across a seam. Fill strips run the same way as the main piece, so a leftover cannot be rotated to fit. That rule creates most of the waste.
Keep seams out of doorways and traffic lanes. A seam in a doorway frays first. Push it under the bed if you can. Our post on carpet seams covers what a good one looks like.
Fill strips go on the least visible side. Under the window or along the closet wall, never down the middle.
Patterns need extra. Every cut lands on the repeat, so pieces get longer.

blocks.text: What we do at the estimate

items.html: Measure every room to the inch, closets and stairs included, and sketch the plan on the spot.
Draw the roll layout and show where each seam falls. If moving one six inches saves a length of roll, we say so.
Quote the measured yardage, not a rounded guess, with the waste visible next to the labor lines. See our carpet installation page.

Flag the two DIY errors we see most. Ordering exactly the square footage, then finding the last bedroom short with no dye-lot match; and measuring a staircase as one flat rectangle when every step needs tread, riser and tuck.

faq.q: How much extra carpet should I order beyond the room's square footage?
faq.a: Plan on 10 to 20 percent for a whole-house job, more for hallways, stairs and rooms just over 12 feet wide. The extra is offcut from the roll and seams that must run with the pile. Note that the waste is carpet you buy, not labor: we bill labor on measured floor.

faq.q: How wide is a roll of carpet?
faq.a: Twelve feet is standard in the United States. Some products come 13 feet 6 inches or 15 feet wide, which can remove a seam in a wider room, but the selection is limited. Confirm the width of the specific carpet before planning a seamless room around it.

faq.q: How much carpet do I need for 13 stairs?
faq.a: Each step uses roughly 20 inches of length once you add tread, riser and tuck, so 13 steps need about 22 feet in a strip slightly wider than the stair. Three strips fit across a 12-foot roll, so plan 7 feet 6 inches of roll. Labor is $30 per step, or $390.

faq.q: Why is carpet sold by the square yard?
faq.a: Tradition from the roll goods trade. One square yard is nine square feet. Many quotes now show square feet instead, so check which unit a quote uses before comparing. Our labor is quoted per square foot of floor: $0.99 stretch-in, $1.29 glue-down, with a 500 sq ft minimum.

faq.q: Can a hallway be carpeted without a seam?
faq.a: Usually yes, if the hall is under 12 feet wide, which nearly all are, and its length fits the roll. Waste is the issue, not the seam: a 3-foot hall from a 12-foot roll leaves 9 feet of width, so a good installer cuts closets and stairs from the same piece.
